subject: Competitive eval + model-quality follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Great chat today — next steps on competitive eval and model-quality tests

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) Goals you shared:
- Replace current inference stack for customer-facing search/summarization (peak TPS ~1200, 99th pctl latency target < 200ms)
- Reduce per-token inference cost while maintaining or improving hallucination rates
- Keep ability to fallback to managed hyperscaler endpoints for peak-burst scenarios

2) What we offered to run for you:
- Competitive eval: run the same eval prompt set across Redwood (open-model variants + quantized variants) and the APIs you mentioned (AWS Bedrock, GCP PaLM API).
- Model-quality comparisons: hallucination/regression checks on a holdout of 500 prompts, plus targeted safety filters.
- Performance matrix: latency/throughput/cost per 1k tokens for each model/hosting mode.

3) Immediate asks for your team: 
- Can you share 100-200 representative prompts and ~20 gold responses for the critical flows (search snippets, product summary generation)? Ideally CSV.
- Any unacceptable hallucination examples or business-critical cases we should prioritize.

4) Timeline: 
- You share sample prompts by EOD Tue (6/16) -> we run initial sweep and share results by Fri (6/18).

Attachments: eval_prompts_v2.csv (sample format), perf_matrix_q2.xlsx (sample output template).

Next steps: I’ll loop in Dylan and Dev to ensure the eval includes exact-match and hallucination heuristics we discussed.

Thanks — looking forward to the data.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0136
[Attachment: eval_prompts_v2.csv (CSV, 14KB)]

From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Great chat today — next steps on competitive eval and model-quality tests

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the concise recap — this looks good. I attached a ZIP with 120 prompts (search/summarize/generation) and about 25 gold responses; flagged 6 examples we consider high-risk for hallucination.

Notes:
- Peak TPS can spike to ~2k for short periods during promos, so please include burst-costs in the perf sheet.
- We're particularly sensitive to product spec hallucinations (inventing features).

I copied Michael (platform engineering) in case you want infra logs or example traces. Looking forward to the results.

Best,
Sarah
Senior PM, Acme Corporation
sarah.jones@acme.com
[Attachment: acme_eval_prompts_20260614.zip (ZIP, 680KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Acme prompts + next steps — need quick test plan

Team — forwarding Acme's prompt bundle (attached). High-level ask: run a cross-model sweep comparing:
- Redwood hosted: rdx-open-3B (float16), rdx-open-7B (int8 quant), rdx-llama-variants (if applicable)
- AWS Bedrock: titan/finetuned variants
- GCP PaLM API: text-bison & fine-tuned if available

Quality checks to include in the first pass:
- Exact-match and token-level overlap vs gold responses
- A conservative hallucination heuristic (named-entity hallucination + factuality mismatch) producing a %rate
- Regression check vs their current baseline (they said the baseline is our competitor X’s managed endpoint)

Please prioritize: 1) hallucination rate on the 6 flagged high-risk prompts, 2) latency p95 for 256-token outputs, 3) cost per 1k tokens estimates for both steady-state and 2k TPS burst scenario.

I’ll coordinate the customer-facing summary. Goal: initial deliverable by 6/18 EOD.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme prompts + next steps — need quick test plan

Got it — plan below and I'll kick off infra today: 

1) Ingest: unzip acme bundle, normalize CSV into prompt_id, prompt_text, gold_response.
2) Run generators: run with same sampling params across endpoints (top_p=0.95, temp=0.0 for deterministic compare where possible; also run jitter/temperature sweep for safety checks).
3) Metrics: compute exact_match, token_overlap (Jaccard), BLEU-ish, and a named-entity hallucination flagger (NER mismatch).
4) Perf: run steady-state throughput tests on Redwood dedicated pool (10 GPU workers), and run API-based synthetic burst tests for Bedrock/PaLM to measure cold/fallback cost.

I’ll attach perf_matrix_q2.xlsx with columns and a short README. If we see >3% hallucination on high-risk prompts we should call it out and offer a mitigation (prefix-based grounding + retrieval).

-Dev
Engineering Lead, Inference
[Attachment: perf_matrix_q2.xlsx (XLSX, 38KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Liu <michael.liu@acme.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Results plan + what you’ll get Friday (6/18)

Hi Sarah —

Quick update: we ingested your bundle and kicked off the cross-model sweep. Early plan for the Friday deliverable (6/18 EOD):

- A short executive summary comparing hallucination rates and latency across Redwood + Bedrock + PaLM.
- Per-prompt heatmap showing where models diverge and the exact flagged hallucination examples.
- Perf matrix with steady-state and burst cost estimates (we'll show cost delta vs your current vendor).
- Recommendations: targeted mitigations (retrieval prompts, prefix grounding, confidence thresholds) and a proposed pilot config for a low-risk rollout.

A couple of quick clarifications that would help the analysis:
- For gold responses: are the 25 golds authoritative (approved by product/legal) or should we treat them as human examples (soft ground truth)?
- Any SLA requirements on 99th pctl latency under 2k TPS bursts? You mentioned 200ms but wanted to confirm if that is strict.

If you prefer, we can do a 20-minute walkthrough of the results on Mon (6/21) to plan the pilot. 

Thanks, and we’ll circulate the deliverable Friday morning PT.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0136
